headline: Free OG Image Generator for Dynamic Social Previews in Next.js
summary: Create custom Open Graph images for link previews with this no-account, no-watermark tool. Supports dynamic generation and Next.js integration.
details: A new free tool allows developers to generate Open Graph (OG) images for social media link previews. It takes a title, subtitle, and color choices to create a 1200x630 PNG, complete with a live URL and matching Next.js code.

OG images are crucial for making shared links visually appealing on platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and messaging apps. The Open Graph protocol, originally from Facebook, ensures consistent display across these services, with X falling back to OG tags if its own are missing.

The recommended size for OG images is 1200x630 pixels (1.91:1 aspect ratio), with files under 5MB. It's important to keep key text within a safe zone of 60-80px padding on all sides to avoid cropping on different devices and platforms.

The generator provides a downloadable PNG, a direct image URL, and a ready-to-use `opengraph-image.tsx` file for Next.js. This file leverages `next/og` to dynamically render images, automatically injecting necessary meta tags into the page head.

For production, using the downloaded PNG or the generated Next.js file ensures independence from third-party URLs. The tool simplifies the process of creating professional-looking link previews, enhancing content sharing across the web.

headline: Waymo partners with Toyota to deploy robotaxis in Japan and the UK
summary: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year, with plans to expand to the UK and other right-hand driving countries.
details: Waymo is expanding its global reach through a new partnership with Toyota, which will supply electric vehicles for robotaxi operations. The companies will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year, with plans to eventually launch a robotaxi service there.

The partnership also aims to deploy these autonomous vehicles in other right-hand driving markets, including the United Kingdom. Waymo has been actively testing its self-driving technology in London and is awaiting necessary permits to launch its service.

Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo's self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. This collaboration builds on a preliminary agreement signed 18 months ago, moving beyond exploratory talks to concrete deployment plans.

Beyond robotaxis, the companies are exploring future initiatives, including bringing Waymo's autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles. They also plan to leverage insights from Waymo's real-world operations to enhance road safety for all users.
